utterances.text: Could you please -- now you see the map P11. Do you see where the port Gruz is located?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. But I cannot orient myself in relation to Srdj and Dubravacka Rijeka, because that helps me locate Luncijata. Because Luncijata is on the forward slope, and that is why I couldn't see it now from this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't be needing the map any more. Could you please take a look at the war log, page 68. Look at the entry at 9.50. It reads here: "Jovanovic: Jovanovic is requesting from the area of Libertas. They are firing upon the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade with the mortars. Jovanovic is asking for 130-millimetres to fire." Is this what you were conveying to the operations centre at the IKM, Kovacevic's request?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the dilemma we were talking about. This was his request. I was conveying it to the operations centre without actually knowing whether they received the request or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, would you please now take a look at your report, under item 2, or rather, I should first ask you the following: This report of the 6th of December, what does it focus on? What does it, for the most part, refer to? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It relates to the preparation of the weapons for the coordination of fire for providing support for the northern part of the Dubrovnik region and the detection of potential targets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, Mr. Jovanovic, in this particular report, under paragraph 2, say that the concept of Captain Kovacevic for the combat activities had been precisely relayed the day before, and do you also mention in that context the commander of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not mention specifically the commander of the 9th VPS, but I rather present the idea that Captain Kovacevic had, envisaging also the concerted action of the artillery units of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, would you look at point 2 and tell me whether there is a word there, KD anti A [phonetic], which would stand for commander here in your report under point 2?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander was mentioned for the following reason. I'm referring you to that earlier discussion we had. On the 5th, as I was leaving the command post, I asked them to inform me once the action was improved [as interpreted] of the time of commencement of the action so that I could prepare myself for the realisation of what had been planned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Under point 6, do you mention the order issued by the warship Captain Milan Zec a day earlier?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the evening before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You don't have to go into detail. We've heard that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think there might be a slight error in the transcript which may need correcting. It says "improved" at line -- 88:25. I think it might mean "approved."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, in this report of 6th December, Exhibit 108, do you mention at all that you had the transfer of duties with the earlier Commander Zdravkovic a couple of days before?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this one of the topics of this report at all?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the following in the same exhibit, 108. There is one rectangular stamp which says "photocopied." But please take a look at it at the other side. Turn the page. Because there it is -- one can see it better. It says there: "Photocopied in copies 1, cabinet NGS." Can you tell us what this stands for?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is short for the chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see the signature down there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is an abbreviation, saying warship captain, and there is an initial there that I cannot read. It is not a signature. These are initials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, finally - because we don't have any more time - I will ask you the following: Prior to your testimony, have you at any time talked to me?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Only with regard to my possible appearance in The Hague as a witness over the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you not tell me that for your own private reasons, and we will not enumerate them here --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I stressed that it was solely for the reasons -- for family reasons that I wasn't prepared to come to The Hague. If you need any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. details, I'm ready to provide them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You avoided the worst of the problem, Mr. Re. And that's enough, is it, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In keeping with the time that you assigned to me, I will finish here with the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Except that you had two and a half times the time I indicated. Mr. Jovanovic, may we thank you very much for your assistance and for the evidence you have given. You are now free to go about your ordinary activities. And may we thank those in Belgrade who have helped with the videolink. Videolink can be closed now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May the Chamber express its appreciation to counsel, especially to the Prosecution, for their preparedness to deal with the cross-examination of this witness today despite the clear difficulties. It has enabled us to conclude that evidence, and it is deeply appreciated. The Chamber would also record its appreciation for the interpreters and other court staff who have been prepared to sit longer than expected to enable this to be concluded. We will resume on Monday afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of July, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.56 p.m.,
